item.title: Climate change threatens malaria elimination in the Asia Pacific.
item.author: Fornace K, Hein PS, Djaafara B, Ashad-Uz-Zaman MN, Chang CC, Elyazar I, Fernandez CD, Hu J, Isa R, Kisomb J, Lim JS, Linn NN, Low A, Manrique E, Maude R, Rocha ICN, Rotejanaprasert C, So-Onguku J, Supriyanto D, Yengmala V, Wan MK, Wulandhari SA, Howard N, Braack L, Mishra S, Mukhtar M.
item.description:
Climate change threatens decades of progress toward malaria elimination across the Asia Pacific. In recent years, reported cases have increased sharply in several regions, including Pakistan following the 2022 floods. However, current research and adaptation strategies have largely focused on gradual warming and shifting transmission seasons and may not fully capture acute operational disruptions in endemic settings. Here we examine how climate change influences malaria through cascading disruptions to health systems, population displacement and ecological change. item.title: 5-year outcomes of chemotherapy de-escalation in HER2-positive early breast cancer and exploratory circulating tumor DNA analyses from the randomized phase 2 PHERGain trial.
item.author: Pérez-García JM, Cortés J, Ruiz-Borrego M, Stradella A, Bermejo B, Escrivá-de-Romaní S, Reboredo C, Albacar C, Martínez-Jáñez N, Iranzo V, Ribelles N, Dalenc F, Prat A, Schmid P, Gebhart G, Marmé F, Di Cosimo S, Braga S, Colleoni M, Antonarelli G, Notini G, Gion M, García-Mosquera JJ, Sanz L, Martinez-Garcia E, Meya A, Dustin D, Amaya-Garrido A, Guerrero-Martínez JA, Alcalá-López D, Rodríguez-Morató J, Mina L, Mancino M, Llombart-Cussac A.
item.description:
PHERGain was a randomized, non-comparative phase 2 trial evaluating a positron 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose-positron emission tomography ( 18 F-FDG-PET)-guided, pathological complete response (pCR)-adapted strategy to omit chemotherapy in HER2-positive early breast cancer. Female patients with HER2-positive stages I-IIIA operable breast cancer (tumor size ≥ 1.5 cm) were randomized to receive chemotherapy plus trastuzumab and pertuzumab (HP; group A) or HP ± endocrine therapy (group B). In group B, treatment was adapted according to 18 F-FDG-PET response after two cycles and pCR, with chemotherapy administered to nonresponders or patients without pCR. We previously reported that this de-escalation approach revealed a 3-year invasive disease-free survival (iDFS) of 94.3% (95% confidence interval (CI): 90.9 to 96.8) in group B. item.title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability.
item.author: Bai Y, Cheng H, Zhou Y, Zhou J, Thirunavukarasu A, Ke Y, Yao J, Fukutsu K, Quek CWN, Hong ASY, Gutierrez L, Berni A, Teo ZL, Ting DSJ, Soetikno BT, Nielsen CS, Elze T, Li Z, Sharma S, Ruthmann N, Linh LD, Chan HH, Koh V, Tan M, Li KZ, Yip L, Cheng CY, Tham YC, Tan GSW, Schmetterer L, Kim RY, Wong D, Ang M, Hussain R, Mehta JS, Aung T, Cheng LT, Tran NTA, Cheng CL, Wong TY, Moshfeghi DM, Liu N, Tan IB, Lim ST, Klang E, Lim TKH, Goh RSM, Liu Y, Ting DSW.
item.description:
Despite their considerable promise, many current medical foundation models remain modality specific and lack transparent reasoning, limiting clinical adoption. To address this gap, we introduce Explainable Vision Language Foundation Model for Medicine (EVLF-FM), a multimodal vision language foundation model that combines broad diagnostic capabilities with fine-grained explainability. The development and testing of EVLF-FM encompassed more than 1.3 million total samples from 18 global datasets across 10 imaging modalities related to six clinical specialties: dermatology, hepatology, ophthalmology, pathology, pulmonology and radiology. External validation employed 13,443 independent test samples from 17 additional datasets across 10 imaging modalities. item.title: Insights into early-onset colorectal cancer from a single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas of colorectal cancer across the age continuum.
item.author: Porter CBM, Murphy SP, Cazaubiel J, Delorey TM, Amir-Zilberstein L, Ashenberg O, Klindziuk L, Andrews E, Tan W, Matsuda K, Kondo A, Ugai S, Ugai T, Ogino S, Finan E, Deguine J, Sicinska E, Brais LK, Thalappillil JS, Giannakis M, Xavier RJ, Anderson AC, Ng K.
item.description:
The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EO-CRC; diagnosed before age 50 years) is increasing worldwide. Although current data indicate that EO-CRC may be biologically distinct from average-onset CRC (AO-CRC; diagnosed at age ≥50 years), molecular differences remain poorly defined. To address this knowledge gap, we generated a single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) atlas from 189 primary CRC tumors (54 EO-CRC, 135 AO-CRC) spanning eight decades of life, with at least 20 tumors in most age decades. Our analyses stratified tumors by microsatellite status and accounted for tumor sidedness, stage, patient sex and neoadjuvant treatment history, modeling age continuously or categorically (EO-CRC versus AO-CRC). item.title: Metabolic heterogeneity of obesity.
item.author: Smith GI, Petersen MC, Hartig SM, Klein S.
item.description:
Multi-organ-system insulin resistance is the key pathogenic driver of obesity-related metabolic complications and diseases, such as atherogenic dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and type 2 diabetes. However, there is considerable heterogeneity in insulin sensitivity among people with obesity. Some are considered to have metabolically healthy obesity, with normal insulin sensitivity in conjunction with normal fasting blood glucose, oral glucose tolerance, plasma lipid profile and intrahepatic triglyceride content. In this Review, we discuss metabolic differences at the cellular, organ-system and systemic levels between people with metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity; we also discuss heterogeneity in the therapeutic effects of weight reduction. item.title: Persistent and compartmentalized T cell immunity in ALS.
item.author: Chen Z, Mansikkaviita J, Seitz C, Yazdani S, Lehikoinen J, Deeba E, Lovik A, Keszei M, Grönlund H, Laaksovirta H, Fang F, Tienari PJ, Ingre C, Andersson J.
item.description:
Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a fatal neurodegenerative disease increasingly linked to T cell responses, although the mechanisms driving T cell activation and disease progression remain unclear. Here we used single-cell RNA and T cell receptor sequencing, longitudinal immune profiling and imaging flow cytometry to identify long-lived intrathecal clonotypes and antigen-presenting cell-T cell complexes displaying features of immunological synapse formation, consistent with intrathecal antigen presentation. Higher frequencies of CD4 + effector, CD4 + regulatory and CD8 + T cells in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) were associated with slower disease progression, whereas increased circulating CD4 + effector and regulatory T cells were associated with faster progression.
